title: VoiceExtractionModel
description: Structured extraction model for spoken agency conversations. Defines what the AI should extract from messy voice/text input to power the THINK IT. SEE IT. pipeline.

projectName.description: The name of the project, campaign, or initiative.
projectName.extractionGuidance: Look for explicit naming ('This is the X project') or infer from context. If multiple names mentioned, use the most recent or most specific.
examples: Brand Relaunch 2025
Summer Campaign
The Trust Project
projectName.ambiguities: Speaker may refer to internal codenames vs. client-facing names. Extract both if present.
projectName.validation: Non-empty string. Flag if not detected — prompt user to confirm.

clientName.description: The client or brand the work is for.
clientName.extractionGuidance: Usually stated early. Look for 'for [client]', 'the client is', or brand name mentions.
examples: Nike
Unilever Home Care
NHS England
clientName.ambiguities: Parent company vs. sub-brand vs. product line. Extract the most specific entity mentioned.
clientName.validation: Non-empty string. Cross-reference with any brand kit loaded.

brief.description: The core brief or task — what the client has asked for, in plain language.
brief.extractionGuidance: Look for 'the brief is', 'they want us to', 'the ask is', 'we need to'. Often stated early but may be refined throughout the conversation. Use the most complete version.
examples: Reposition the brand for a younger audience without alienating existing customers
Create a launch campaign for a new product line entering a crowded market
Develop a thought leadership platform that establishes the CEO as an industry voice
brief.ambiguities: Speaker may describe the brief indirectly ('they're struggling with X' = the brief is to solve X). Multiple briefs may be mentioned — extract the primary one and note secondary asks.
brief.validation: Required. Must be at least 10 words. If not detected, the pipeline cannot proceed — prompt user.

audience.description: Who the work is for — the people it needs to reach and move.

examples: Gen Z women 18–24 who are fitness-curious but gym-averse
CFOs at mid-market SaaS companies making platform decisions

demographics.description: Age, gender, income, geography — whatever was mentioned.

psychographics.description: Values, attitudes, beliefs, lifestyle — the deeper profile.

behaviours.description: What they do — media habits, purchase patterns, cultural participation.

audience.extractionGuidance: Listen for 'the audience is', 'we're talking to', 'these people', 'the target'. Speakers often describe audiences through stories or stereotypes — extract the underlying profile.
audience.ambiguities: Internal stakeholders (the people approving the work) vs. external audience (the people seeing the work). Extract external audience as primary. Note internal stakeholders separately if mentioned.
audience.validation: Required. At minimum, primary audience must be populated.

challenge.description: The core business, brand, or communication challenge the work must overcome.
challenge.extractionGuidance: Look for 'the problem is', 'the challenge is', 'what's hard is', 'the tension is'. Often stated as a frustration or complaint. May need to be synthesized from multiple scattered mentions.
examples: The brand is seen as outdated by younger consumers but can't afford to lose its loyal base
Low awareness in a saturated category where every competitor says the same thing
Internal misalignment between what the brand promises and what the product actually delivers
challenge.ambiguities: Speakers often conflate symptoms (low sales) with root causes (irrelevant positioning). Extract the deeper challenge, not just the surface symptom.
challenge.validation: Required. Must be a substantive statement, not just 'sales are down'.

problem.description: The specific problem to be solved — more tactical than the challenge.
problem.extractionGuidance: Distinguish from challenge: challenge is strategic ('brand relevance'), problem is tactical ('need a campaign by Q3'). May overlap.
examples: Need to launch in 6 markets simultaneously with a single creative platform
The website doesn't convert because the value proposition is unclear
problem.ambiguities: May be identical to challenge for simpler briefs. Extract separately only if the speaker distinguishes them.
problem.validation: Optional. If identical to challenge, merge.

marketContext.description: The competitive, cultural, and market landscape.

categoryState.description: Overall state of the category (e.g., 'commoditized', 'rapidly growing', 'declining trust')

marketContext.extractionGuidance: Listen for competitor names, category descriptions, trend references. Speakers often reference competitors indirectly ('everyone else is doing X').
marketContext.ambiguities: Aspirational competitors (who they want to be like) vs. direct competitors (who they compete with). Extract both and label.
marketContext.validation: Optional but strongly recommended for strategy decks.

insight.description: The core human, cultural, or market insight that unlocks the strategy. The single most important extraction for creative work.
insight.extractionGuidance: Listen for 'the insight is', 'what we found is', 'the truth is', 'people don't realize'. Also listen for anecdotes, stories, or observations that reveal a deeper truth. The insight is often the thing the speaker gets most animated about.
examples: People don't want to be healthy — they want to feel in control
In B2B, the real decision-maker isn't the buyer — it's the person who has to use the product daily
Luxury used to mean exclusion. Now it means access to experiences others can't get.
insight.ambiguities: Data points are not insights. 'Sales are up 20%' is data. 'People buy more when they feel part of a community' is an insight. Extract the human truth, not the statistic.
insight.validation: Optional but critical for quality. If not stated, the system should attempt to synthesize one from the available inputs and flag it as 'system-generated' for user review.

opportunity.description: The strategic opportunity the brand can own.
opportunity.extractionGuidance: Look for 'the opportunity is', 'the white space is', 'nobody is doing', 'we could own'. Often framed as a gap between what exists and what could exist.
examples: No brand in the category speaks to the emotional side of the decision — everyone leads with features
There's a cultural shift toward transparency that this brand is uniquely positioned to lead
opportunity.ambiguities: Opportunity vs. insight: insight is the truth, opportunity is what you do with it. They're related but distinct.
opportunity.validation: Optional. If not extracted, can be generated from insight + challenge.

proposition.description: The core brand or campaign proposition — the single organising thought.
proposition.extractionGuidance: Listen for 'the proposition is', 'the idea is', 'the territory is', 'the positioning is'. Usually stated concisely. If the speaker rambles, extract the tightest version.
examples: Own the conversation about responsible innovation
Make fitness feel like self-care, not self-punishment
The bank that proves trust, not just promises it
proposition.ambiguities: Proposition vs. tagline vs. campaign idea. Proposition is the strategic thought. Tagline is the expression. Campaign idea is the creative execution. Extract the proposition specifically.
proposition.validation: Optional. For pitch decks and campaign decks, this is critical.

risk.description: How creatively brave this territory is

ideaTerritories.description: Creative territories or directions mentioned or implied.
ideaTerritories.extractionGuidance: Listen for 'we could go in the direction of', 'one route might be', 'what if we'. Speakers often float ideas without labelling them as territories — extract and name them.
ideaTerritories.ambiguities: Half-formed ideas vs. deliberate territories. Extract anything that sounds like a creative direction, even if embryonic.
ideaTerritories.validation: Optional. Used to seed creative route generation.

proof.description: Evidence, data points, or proof points mentioned.
proof.extractionGuidance: Listen for statistics, research references, case studies, benchmarks, test results. Also extract anecdotal evidence and expert opinions.
examples: NPS increased 15 points after the last campaign
According to Kantar, trust in the category is at an all-time low
We tested this concept with 200 users and 78% preferred it

constraints.extractionGuidance: Listen for 'we can't', 'the budget is', 'by when', 'they won't approve', 'we have to include'. Constraints are often mentioned casually — capture them all.
constraints.validation: Optional. Each constraint should be actionable.

unknowns.description: Things the speaker doesn't know yet — gaps, open questions, pending research.
unknowns.extractionGuidance: Listen for 'I'm not sure', 'we need to find out', 'TBD', 'the question is', 'we're waiting on'. Also infer unknowns from vague statements.
examples: We don't know the exact media budget yet
Still waiting on consumer research from the client
Not sure if the CEO will approve anything bold
unknowns.validation: Optional. Surfacing unknowns early improves deck quality.

tone.description: Desired tonal direction for the work.

references.description: Tonal references — brands, campaigns, or cultural touchpoints cited

tone.extractionGuidance: Listen for 'the tone should be', 'like [reference]', 'not too [attribute]', 'think [brand/campaign]'. Also infer tone from the speaker's own energy and language.
tone.validation: Optional. Defaults to 'Confident and clear' if not specified.

desiredOutcome.description: What the speaker wants to achieve with this presentation specifically.
desiredOutcome.extractionGuidance: Listen for 'the goal is', 'we need them to', 'by the end they should', 'we want approval for'. This is about the presentation's purpose, not the campaign's KPIs.
examples: Get the CMO to approve the creative route so we can move to production
Align the internal team on the strategy before the client presentation
Win the pitch — this is competitive, three agencies
desiredOutcome.ambiguities: Campaign outcomes (increase sales) vs. presentation outcomes (get approval). Extract the presentation outcome.
desiredOutcome.validation: Optional but helps the system choose the right deck type and tone.

deckType.description: The type of deck needed. May be stated or inferred.
deckType.extractionGuidance: Listen for 'pitch deck', 'strategy presentation', 'workshop'. If not stated, infer from context: competitive = pitch, alignment = strategy, launch = campaign, internal = workshop.
deckType.validation: Optional. System should infer if not stated.

rawConfidence.description: Confidence scores for each extraction field.
Per-field confidence (0–1) to help the UI surface low-confidence extractions for user review.
